source.title: Over-parametrized neural networks as under-determined linear systems
source.authors: Austin R. Benson; Anil Damle; Alex Townsend

page_placements.theme: Fitting effort depends on geometry, target complexity and optimization

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no obvious cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: Studies whether simple networks can achieve zero training loss, but uses a fixed random-features model and conditioning/optimization analysis rather than the original deep-network random-label experiments. It also gives counterexamples for bias-free ReLU and swish.
record.gate_note: Reports own results on fitting arbitrary labels in a two-layer, single-hidden-layer setup and on cases where fitting is impossible; reports no tests using completely random labels, shuffled or noise inputs, test error, or generalization on true labels. Synthetic-2 labels are stated as 50 positive and 50 negative, not as random labeling. Results about cited prior work are not rows. Figure-only conditioning plots are not extracted as numeric result rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes interpolation and conditioning in single-hidden-layer networks, principally with fixed random features. Its experiments use real regression targets or structured labels, and its arbitrary-label theorems concern a different model class from the standard deep networks in V1. Neither absolute convergence times nor kernel singularity test the random-versus-true-label comparisons in V2. The bias-free shallow-network counterexample does not contradict V1 in its stated scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors explain zero training loss in simple random-feature networks through underdetermined linear systems, identify bias-free ReLU and swish interpolation obstructions, and connect conditioning to gradient-descent behavior. They emphasize that training loss alone cannot distinguish learned models and explicitly omit generalization analysis.
record.recipe_differences: A theoretical and numerical study of two-layer, single-hidden-layer random-feature networks; freezes hidden weights for its principal zero-loss analysis, uses regression datasets and a constructed rank-deficient counterexample, and explicitly omits generalization analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Activation function and dataset affect whether the feature/kernel matrix is singular and how well-conditioned it is; width affects Wendland conditioning; the paper reports that jointly training hidden weights increased the condition number in Synthetic-1.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a positive-definite population feature matrix and sufficient width, last-layer gradient descent converges to a zero-loss least-norm solution for arbitrary targets with probability at least 1 − δ.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide single-hidden-layer random-feature networks can interpolate arbitrary targets under explicit feature-rank and step-size conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: A constructed eight-point set makes bias-free shallow ReLU features rank deficient for every width and hidden-weight choice; related ReLU kernels and swish features are also singular.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bias-free single-hidden-layer ReLU and swish models have structural obstructions to interpolating arbitrary targets on some distinct-point datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: On Prostate-Cancer regression, Wendland activations require tens of thousands of steps, ReLU over a million, and swish does not converge within 10 million.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-dependent conditioning can make fixed-feature regression convergence slow even in highly overparameterized networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly training hidden and output weights increases the feature-matrix condition number on Synthetic-1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint weight training need not improve feature-matrix conditioning.

record.problems: The positive zero-loss results concern a simple two-layer scalar-output model with fixed random features, not standard deep networks on image classification. No random-label experiment, test error, or generalization measurement is reported. Several convergence observations are described from figures without exact terminal errors; theoretical guarantees require λmin(H)>0 and a stated width bound.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 conditioning quantiles and Figure 3 spectral/filter plots are figure-only properties rather than training-error or random-label outcomes. Figure 4 shows condition number growth, recorded in R10; no numeric values are stated. No cited prior-study results were included.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks under unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters, and chance-level test performance.
Training-time ratio for random versus true labels and convergence changes across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: Random hidden weights are not random labels. Arbitrary-target interpolation theorems are relevant background, but their shallow fixed-feature scope does not establish the versions supplied here. Synthetic-2 assigns all eight counterexample points label +1; rank deficiency alone therefore does not establish failure to fit that experiment's particular target vector.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report a completely random labeling experiment, test error at chance, or true-label generalization. The positive zero-loss result is conditional on an activation/kernel with positive minimum eigenvalue and sufficiently large width; ReLU and swish have a counterexample dataset.

No comparison of training time for true versus random labels, or sweep over corruption fractions. Reports slow convergence and failure to converge within stated iteration counts for some activations in one dataset.
No shuffled pixels, permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep over fractions of corrupted labels and no corresponding test-error measurements.
No comparison of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation as regularizers for fitting random labels or generalizing on true labels.
No training-time comparison of learning real patterns versus noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: two-layer neural network with Wendland0 activation, fixed random hidden weights
rows.size_stated: width m satisfying m ≥ 10nC² log(2n/δ)/λmin(H); numerical experiment uses m = 200n
rows.operation_detail: Trained only the last linear layer by gradient descent with hidden weights fixed at random initialization.

conditions.value: as in Lemma 4.2 for the numerical experiment

rows.measure: Training error / relative error during optimization
rows.value: Eventually converges to zero training error theoretically under Theorem 4.3 assumptions; numerical experiment reports tens of thousands of gradient descent steps for convergence.
rows.uncertainty: Theorem 4.3 gives probability at least 1 − δ; numerical uncertainty not stated in text.
rows.note: This concerns the paper's regression targets on a small single-hidden-layer model, not random image labels. The finite experiment's exact terminal error is not stated in prose.
rows.check: Combines a general conditional theorem with a Prostate-Cancer experiment using real regression targets. Neither measures random-label fitting by standard deep networks; the numerical terminal error is not specified in prose.

rows.measure: Training error / relative error during optimization
rows.value: Eventually converges to zero training error theoretically under Theorem 4.3 assumptions; numerical experiment reports tens of thousands of gradient descent steps for convergence.

rows.value: Over a million steps for convergence; the ReLU example eventually converges on this dataset.

rows.subject: two-layer neural network with swish activation, fixed random hidden weights
rows.size_stated: width m = 200n in the numerical experiment
rows.operation_detail: Trained only the last linear layer by gradient descent with hidden weights fixed at random initialization.
rows.measure: Training error / relative error during optimization
rows.value: Does not converge after 10 million steps; error decrease stagnates after just 20 iterations.
rows.note: A convergence limitation for the tested real-target regression setup. It does not test random-label fitting.
rows.check: Failure to converge within 10 million steps concerns real-target regression with fixed features. It cannot establish absence or incompleteness of V1 or V2.

rows.subject: bias-free single-hidden-layer neural network with ReLU activation
rows.operation_detail: Proved the feature matrix has rank at most 7 on a specified eight-point dataset, regardless of hidden weights.
rows.measure: Rank of feature matrix; ability to interpolate arbitrary labels
rows.baseline: full row rank would permit interpolation; no numeric baseline stated
rows.value: Feature matrix rank at most 7; some label vectors cannot achieve zero error regardless of width or training.
rows.note: This is a theoretical counterexample on a specially constructed dataset, not a random-label image experiment.
rows.check: Valid interpolation counterexample for a bias-free single-hidden-layer ReLU model, but outside V1's stated system class. Inability to interpolate some labels is not a reversed random-label effect.

rows.subject: bias-free single-hidden-layer neural network with ReLU activation
rows.size_stated: any finite width m and infinite-width limit
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed the population feature Gram matrix on the specified eight-point dataset.
rows.baseline: nonsingular H is the condition used for the zero-loss guarantee
rows.note: The stated singularity implies the paper's full-row-rank guarantee does not apply to this dataset.
rows.check: Population Gram-matrix singularity is a structural result for the shallow bias-free model, not a measurement of V1. It largely restates the obstruction in R5.

rows.subject: bias-free single-hidden-layer neural network with ReLU activation
rows.size_stated: any finite width m and infinite-width limit
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed the ReLU neural tangent kernel matrix on the specified eight-point dataset.
rows.baseline: nonsingular G is the comparison reference; numeric baseline not stated
rows.value: The 8 × 8 matrix G and its finite-width counterpart are singular.
rows.note: The authors state the point set causes both matrices to be singular.
rows.check: NTK singularity on the constructed point set does not measure random-label training error in standard deep networks; reversed is inappropriate.

rows.subject: bias-free single-hidden-layer neural network with swish activation
rows.size_stated: any finite width m and infinite-width limit
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed the population feature Gram matrix on the specified eight-point dataset.
rows.measure: Singularity of population matrix H and feature rank
rows.baseline: full row rank would permit interpolation; no numeric baseline stated
rows.value: The matrix H is singular and the feature matrix does not have full row rank on the same point set.
rows.note: A specified counterexample, not a random-label image experiment.
rows.check: Swish singularity and feature-rank deficiency concern the shallow bias-free model and constructed inputs, outside V1's scope; reversed is inappropriate.

rows.subject: two-layer neural network with Wendland activation, fixed random hidden weights
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes zero-loss least-norm solution for last-layer gradient descent with fixed random features.
rows.measure: Existence and convergence to zero objective value
rows.value: Unique least-norm solution achieves zero objective with probability at least 1 − δ; gradient descent converges as k → ∞.
rows.uncertainty: failure probability δ; probability at least 1 − δ
rows.note: The theorem covers any labels y under its assumptions, but does not test random labels or images.
rows.check: Theorem 4.3 guarantees interpolation of arbitrary targets for a conditional fixed-feature shallow model, rather than V1's standard deep networks. Its activation assumption is any qualifying gamma with positive minimum population eigenvalue, not exclusively Wendland.

rows.subject: two-layer neural network with jointly trained ReLU hidden and last-layer weights
rows.operation_detail: Jointly trained W and α using a stochastic gradient method.
rows.measure: Condition number of γ(WᵀX) during training
rows.note: This measures conditioning, not time to fit random labels or convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
rows.check: Condition-number growth during learning of structured Synthetic-1 targets does not measure either component of V2.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study discusses prior zero-training-loss findings and their interpretation without testing the specified random-label claims or using random-label memorization as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study analyzes interpolation and optimization in single-hidden-layer random-feature networks. Its experiments do not test random-label fitting or true-label versus random-label convergence, and its conditional arbitrary-target theorem does not establish any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Theorem 4.3 gives conditional asymptotic convergence with probability at least 1 − δ; Figure 2 uses width m = 200n. Prostate-Cancer targets are log antigen levels, and generalization is explicitly outside the study's scope.
